topic: What is the future of hydrogen energy?
research_question: Under which combinations of hydrogen production pathways, renewable and firm electricity, storage, transport infrastructure, end-use conversion, and policy support does hydrogen deliver additional climate, reliability, industrial, or energy-access value compared with direct electrification and competing fuels, after accounting for lifecycle emissions, water, land, energy losses, leakage, safety, cost, and demand uncertainty?

candidate_routes.name: industrial_feedstock_replacement
candidate_routes.reason: uses existing chemical demand and infrastructure while testing displacement, certification, and lifecycle emissions

candidate_routes.name: hydrogen_direct_reduction_and_high_temperature_industry
candidate_routes.reason: targets processes where molecular or high-temperature service may outperform direct electricity

candidate_routes.name: hydrogen_derived_transport_fuels
candidate_routes.reason: tests shipping, aviation-derived fuels, and heavy transport with full conversion-chain accounting

candidate_routes.name: long_duration_and_seasonal_storage
candidate_routes.reason: tests whether duration and transportability offset lower round-trip efficiency

candidate_routes.name: remote_resilience_and_backup
candidate_routes.reason: tests low-utilization reserve value under severe outages and local logistics

candidate_routes.name: coordinated_hydrogen_hubs
candidate_routes.reason: integrates production, offtake, storage, transport, flexible power demand, safety, and staged adoption

falsifiable_claims: annual grid emissions can misstate electrolysis benefits
production without offtake and infrastructure is not viability
lifecycle and safety constraints can reorder pathways
required_boundaries: hydrogen is an energy carrier and feedstock
separate color labels from lifecycle accounting
include leakage safety water materials and demand uncertainty
